messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] data convesion
parts:
Each row in the cross info file has a MAGIC line's ID followed by a permutation of the integers 1-8 to indicate the order of the crosses among the 8 founder lines that gave rise to that founder line.

From your pedigree file it's a bit tricky to trace the lines back to the 8 founders, but I wrote an R function to do so:
https://gist.github.com/kbroman/a5ce0d6db218290736cf27d816191705#file-ped2crossinfo-r

Here's a portion of the output, available at https://gist.github.com/kbroman/a5ce0d6db218290736cf27d816191705

6435,7,1,8,6,5,4,3,2
...
6439,5,3,4,2,8,7,6,1
...
6450,8,7,6,1,4,3,5,2
...
6458,5,4,3,2,7,6,8,1
...
6467,7,6,8,1,4,3,5,2
6468,7,6,8,1,4,3,5,2
6469,7,6,8,1,4,3,5,2
6470,7,6,8,1,4,3,5,2
6471,7,6,8,1,4,3,5,2
6472,7,6,8,1,4,3,5,2

I would subset that file to the rows that correspond to the MAGIC lines for which you have genotype and phenotype data.

Kind regards,
karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] data convesion
parts:
Also note that I just found bugs in the transition probabilities for 8-way RIL by selfing (and also 4- and 16-way RIL by selfing).
You can install the corrected R/qtl2 package with

devtools::install_github("kbroman/qtl2")

I also tried to add a bit more explanation about the cross information for multi-way RIL in the "input file format" document:

http://kbroman.org/qtl2/assets/vignettes/input_files.html#multi-parent_recombinant_inbred_lines

karl
